text:
claire_dev: reproducible weirdness using the Python async SDK against a Dedicated/private endpoint behind a local sidecar proxy + custom CA. curl with --cacert works but the async sample fails with certificate verify error. :confused:

claire_dev: async repro snippet (simplified):
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://private.internal:8443", api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
await client.chat.create("hi")
```

claire_dev: container has /etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem mounted and I can do: `curl --cacert /etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem https://private.internal:8443/api/health` and it succeeds. httpx in the async client raises `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed`

ben_platform: two things to try: 1) httpx can pick up HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY via trust_env. that may cause an extra proxy layer to attempt its own TLS handling. 2) httpx uses its own SSLContext unless explicitly passed. try disabling env proxy parsing or provide ssl context.

ben_platform: quick workaround that fixed it for me:
```py
import ssl
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ssl_ctx.load_verify_locations('/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://private.internal:8443', api_key=..., ssl=ssl_ctx, trust_env=False)
```

claire_dev: that moves past the handshake. two follow-ups: docs don't show ssl param usage, and our retry layer is currently retrying on SSL errors which obscures the root cause in logs (retries + backoff then final failure).

maria_onboard: we only have the simple quickstart in onboarding. we should add a short dedicated/private section: proxy + custom CA + note about trust_env. include the explicit sample and demo docker-compose.

ryan_sre: agreed on retries: the retry predicate currently treats any transport-related exception as retryable. ssl.SSLError from verify failure shouldn't be retried. i'll open an issue to exclude verification failures from retry. also caller-facing logs should indicate "non-retryable SSL verification failure" to avoid confusion.

ben_platform: small SDK improvements proposed: 1) expose ssl: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] parameter on AsyncClient constructor and in typed stubs, 2) ensure AsyncClient.__aenter__ returns the concrete client type in .pyi/stubs so context manager usage is typed (mypy folks keep tripping on this), 3) update docs and add example under examples/dedicated-proxy-ca.

claire_dev: i'll draft the docs PR and attach a tiny example repo (Dockerfile + compose + env var notes). will include failing httpx stacktrace + successful curl command and the env vars I used: HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. note: httpx respects trust_env so environment proxy/certs matter unless trust_env=False.

deploy-bot: pushed branch feat/dedicated-proxy-ca-doc by claire_dev to staging/docs (CI queued) :rocket:

ben_platform: i'll prepare the SDK PR. unit test plan: simulate ssl.SSLError raised on first attempt and assert no retry attempts are made (mock transport). also add typing change to AsyncClient context manager return type.

ryan_sre: extra FYI for infra teams: if you're using envoy/sidecar + HTTP_PROXY in k8s, mounting the CA and forcing explicit ssl context or disabling trust_env is the practical workaround. envoy's interception can make curl behave differently depending on flags.

maria_onboard: cc @docs — if you can help craft clear onboarding wording that avoids scary "SSL" jargon for devs, that would be great. include a checklist: mount CA, set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for sync requests, pass ssl context or set trust_env=False for async httpx flows.

claire_dev: thanks all, will open both PRs (docs + SDK) and link back here. saved us a half day. :tada:
